articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of the Use of the Internet of Things in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The application of precision agriculture is presented with the objective of spatially and temporally optimizing the life cycle of different crops through technologies, to increase the productivity of agricultural enterprises. In this article, a bibliometric analysis was performed, where a trend study of publications was carried out, extracting the main characteristics of the topic. We also made use of the statistical tool Rstudio together with the Scopus database, where we analyzed about the most relevant sources published from 2010 to 2021 and the exact number of sources published on precision agriculture and IoT. In addition, the most cited articles worldwide on the topic and the production profile by authors and areas (Thematic) indicating the total number of articles published for precision agriculture, agriculture, IoT, etc. are analyzed. This shows that precision agriculture has had a greater impact in Asia and India.

articleTitle: Very-Short Term Electricity Demand Forecasting Integrating Solar Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents different mathematical models to integrate solar distributed generation (DG) into very-short term demand forecasting processes in Colombia. The proposed models can forecast up to 4032 5-minute periods (two weeks) of net demand. To do so, historical data, calendar effects and meteorological data have been considered to define mathematical models. Also, different strategies and models like recurrent neural networks, generalized additive models, and ordinary least squares to incorporate the effect of solar DG have been carefully evaluated and compared. Multiple scenarios of solar DG penetration levels, previously elaborated by “The Minning and Energy Planning Unit (UPME)”, have been analyzed in order to explore the potential future advantages and drawbacks of the employed models and strategies. Results have shown that our models can forecast 4032 periods of net demand with MAPEs within 1.29% and 3.8%.

articleTitle: Covid-19 Projections: A Simple Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: We present a straightforward way to produce Covid-19 projections by using a machine learning method. Incident and cumulative data for confirmed infected, deaths and vaccinated in Mexico during 2021, are employed to obtain useful projections by using Wolfram Mathematica and Matlab<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> regression learner app.

articleTitle: IoT stations for monitoring a district metered area of Guanajuato city
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the first phase toward the implementation of a monitoring and diagnostic pilot system for a district metered area (DMA) of the water distribution network (WDN) of Guanajuato city. Such a system consists of two main components: (1) a grid of stations equipped with Internet of Things (IoT) technology, where hydraulic and quality data are measured and sent to a web platform, and (2) algorithms based on artificial intelligence and control theory for providing early diagnosis of faults and quality deviations. Specifically, this work describes the architecture and installation of the first and second stations, which were located at the DMA input and in a public hospital. Moreover, some preliminary uses of the recollected data are presented to show the potentiality of metering drinking water.

articleTitle: Automatic Segmentation of Lateral Ventricles in MRI of Pediatric Patients from 4 to 12 Months
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The utilization of image processing tools for magnetic resonance image (MRI) processing has made possible carrying out the study of injuries and diseases, as it facilitates the look up of the information contained in the image. The objective of this work is the implementation of a digital image processing methodology to perform the segmentation of lateral ventricles in MRI images of pediatric patients using automatic thresholding techniques, contour detection, and morphological operators. The segmentation algorithms efficacy is evaluated with the support of a specialist, resulting in an 82% of efficiency in the segmentation of the lateral ventricles. On the other hand, the average processing time is 4.79 seconds. With these results, the study allows establishing the effectiveness of the automatic calculation of thresholds, as well as the use of contour extraction algorithms, and morphological operators as support tools that accentuates the validity of the segmentation model.

articleTitle: Advanced Power Generation & Demand Forecasting Considering the Complete Energy Matrix using an Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper introduces the application of an Artificial Neural Network to perform the power generation & demand forecasting of a regional electricity network. The main technical contribution of this article is the consideration of many variables (35) that involve the complete energy matrix information to calculate the generated and demanded power accurately. The final results showed that the related correlation factor of the net generation forecast and net demand forecast using Artificial Neural Network are very adequate (greater than 0.95). Furthermore, the percentage of error between the predicted value and the actual power generation and demand values is reduced (up to 0.22 %). Finally, the results of the long-term forecast (up to 30 days) also proved to be adequate considering the correlation factor and percentage of error associated with the power generation and demand forecast.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of reduced diode clamped multilevel inverter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The design of a new single-phase multilevel inverter is presented, using the type of diode clamped with reduced devices, a comparison control algorithm is used, the inverter must present characteristics in its performance parameters using IEEE Std. 519 as reference, two configurations are proposed to work: powered by 12 and 24 V series battery array, the proposed design and the control algorithm are simulated in Matlab.

articleTitle: Wireless System Design for Direct Current Photoplethysmography
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: A recent report showed that an OPT-101 photodetector and a red light-emitting diode (LED) of 630 nm wavelength could be employed to detect direct current Photoplethysmography (DC-PPG) signals and their associated hemodynamic responses in the in-vivo exposed spinal cord and brainstem. This work describes the design of a wireless system that allows to measure and transmit these low intensity DC - PPG signals successfully to a receiving stage located at a fixed length of 10 m. To obtain several low-intensity DC-PPG signals to be wirelessly transmitted and detected at the reception stage, we positioned the OPT-101 photodetector at different distances from the LED, from 0 to 30 cm. We show that our wireless system was capable of detecting all of these transmitted DC-PPG signals. As expected, we found a decrease in the OPT-101 voltage output and its associated wireless potential depending on the distance from 0 to 30 cm, showing a similar behavior. We suggest that different arrangements of our device could be employed to wirelessly detect hemodynamic responses in the spinal cord and brain in various animal models and in the human brain.

articleTitle: Graphical user interface for marine propeller optimum diameter estimation using MyOpenLab
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Generally selection of optimum propeller diameter is quite elaborate to naval architects in the preliminary design stage. Implementing a Graphical User Interface (GUI) can facilitate the user to decrease time in the calculation process and obtain a first adequate approximation. For diameter prediction, a practical approach based on empirical equations was used based on Wageningen B-series charts, the most widely used systematic propeller series nowadays, because of its data fidelity from open water model tests. The design of the GUI is developed using the open-source software MyOpenLab<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> for graphical and modular programming. The results obtained from the GUI are compared with those of an example from literature and good agreement between the data is observed.

articleTitle: User interface for calculation of principal stresses and Mohr’s Circle
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The implementation of calculation tools is an efficient way to solve problems in education and professional practice. The user interface developed, for teaching purposes, in the MyOpenLab graphic programming software, allows the calculation of the plane stress states as a function of the principal stresses and the maximum shear stress, in addition to obtaining the values of the stresses corresponding to a specific direction entered by the user. The graphical representation of the stress states is also provided in a general way, as well as the Mohr’s circle and the location of their respective parameters.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of a hybrid aSi:H/CH3NH3PbI3 heterojunction solar cell
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted great attention as low-cost and high-power conversion efficiency (PCE) emerging devices. Usually, the PSCs consists of a three-layer n-i-p structure, where the i layer corresponds to a perovskite and the n and p layers to n-type and p-type semiconductors, respectively. Toward a higher solar cell cost reduction, in this work a bilayer perovskite p-n solar cell configuration using aSi:H (p) is proposed. The functionality of the proposed device is demonstrated by employing numerical simulations. The optimal thickness of Perovskite (CH3NH3PbI3) to obtain the maximum solar cell efficiency is also determined. Finally, we analyze the effect of the density of trap states in the perovskite on the device’s open-circuit voltage.

articleTitle: Complementary Statistical Models for the Determination of Foundry Temperatures in the Fourth Segment of the L+Fe3C Region in the Iron–Carbon Phase Diagram
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The analyzed segment belongs to the L+Fe3C region, this segment is constituted by a range of carbon content of 6.10% (lower) and 6.67% in the upper limit. In other words, it is the fourth segment of the region. To estimate the melting temperatures, an iterative procedure was used, which has been shown to be complex to determine intermediate values in the thermal range, specialists in statistical modeling have developed new estimation methods, following the trend, this article presents three complementary models statistics which can be used to know any temperature value in the fourth segment of the analyzed region, without the need to carry out the iterative procedure and optimizing the statistical model that has been designed for this segment, the proposed models are of the linear and polynomial type, with significantly positive coefficients of without manifestation of discordant data, these models are valid for predicting temperatures and present lower uncertainties compared to the iterative method and the statistical model previously proposed.

articleTitle: Digital Utilities for Sustainable Constructions at Landfills Supporting Safe Community Health Infrastructures and Humanity Protection in Risk at post COVID-19 era
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The current study presents useful digital monitoring tools for environmental impact assessment, sustainable development, safe infrastructures related to sustainable tourism, heritage and cultural tourism monuments, archaeological sites, water resources sports tourism sites, ecological landscape tourism sites close to landfill sites. Useful tools are presented for stakeholders examining particular digital utilities for decision making to mitigate toxic hazardous probable landfill gas’s atmospheric pollution concentrations from landfill sites. In this paper are presented useful digital utilities as a framework of an integrated community health policy to support safe construction designs and proper monitoring schemes for public health protection and efficient economic designs. Integrated public health policy is presented within useful digital utilities applying proper management techniques for monitoring landfill emissions and decision making protecting community health and public health. Useful results are presented for sustainable construction facilities next to landfill sites that promote sustainable tourism, cultural – heritage tourism, sports tourism, ecological tourism and safety of associated community health infrastructures at post COVID-19 era within renewable resources from treated landfill emissions, green circular economy, clean technologies.

Author Keywords: digital utilities for safe constructions protecting humanity in risk at post COVID-19 era

articleTitle: Edpuzzle and Canvas as distance learning tools during the lockdown
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The following study was carried out during the teaching-learning process in the Tec21 educational model of Tecnológico de Monterrey (Mexico), an educational model based on challenges, during confinement forced by a pandemic in 2020. Specifically, it shows how Edpuzzle and Canvas applications are tools that improve motivation and understanding of topics in the online teaching process during the COVID-19 pandemic and how these resources can successfully change traditional education to a distance learning system with the help of online classes. In this study, the perceptions of university students about the use of the Edpuzzle application together with the Canvas learning management system were explored to identify if students consider that it favors the educational process and to know if it motivates the learning of basic sciences in the first years semesters of a university degree during confinement. Qualitative data were collected from new university students (n=163). The results show that Edpuzzle and Canvas contributed as a motivational element and as a cognitive resource, positively impacting student performance.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis from table of offsets in hydrostatic calculations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Naval architects and marine engineers are aware of the benefits of using programming software to solve complex math calculations from a numerical computer system. The purpose of this work is to show how MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software can be used to do hydrostatic calculations with the use of integration methods by shaping curves of a vessel, due to its great importance in stability calculations and in phases design. The use of these tools is quite beneficial in supporting computer-assisted education, chiefly, owing to optimization of time required to solve complex operations; furthermore, helping along to engineering students in the performance of projects and serving as support in the naval technical area as an alternative of the application software.

articleTitle: Experimenting blended learning in a flipped classroom environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The synergy of blended learning and flipped classroom educational models have been in great demand in recent years, especially as a result of the COVID-19 coronavirus pandemic that has forced traditional education to implement alternative models that make use of information technologies to continue the academic training of students worldwide at all educational levels. The objective of this research was to validate the relevance of the implementation of blended learning in a flipped classroom environment in a higher education course. The research methodology was quantitative, using the survey as an instrument. The results obtained are concentrated in a great acceptance of the applied models indicating ease in the learning scheme and the improvement in the autonomy of the students through the virtual platform, the need for adequate planning and design of the course is asserted, in addition The guidance, intervention and feedback of the teacher as facilitator of the course was essential. As a consequence of this, its validation allows endless opportunities for the design of educational experiences under these teaching models, since it can be implemented in other areas of knowledge.

articleTitle: Methane Gas (CH4) detection using an (EGFET) Extended Gate CMOS microsensor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: To reduce the number of fatal accidents in hostile and dangerous environments for humans, today, it is necessary to harmful gases measure using portable systems that employ sensors based on microelectronics. Therefore, in this work, the main structure of an extended gate CMOS microsensor is presented where a vanadium oxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) layer has been incorporated as a methane gas (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) detection membrane to analyze the behavior of the proposed device. The complete microsensor is composed of an NMOS transistor and an extended gate (EGFET), using 0.5 μm ON Semiconductor CMOS processess, with V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> bias voltages less than 1 V and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> voltage less than 1 V, for it to work in the linear region. Preliminary results performed in TopSPICE software showing an optimal behavior. I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> vs V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> characteristics curve simulations of the layout and 2D numerical simulations with the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensitive membrane film using the silvaco TCAD software are presented.

articleTitle: Implementation of a technique for obstacle detection applied to Resistive Grid Path Planning Methodology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Path planning has been considered an import part of solving problems focused on collision-free movements for robotics system. Resistive Grid Path Planning Methodology (RGPPM) is a novel and reduced CPU time modelling procedure for robotic motions planning. In this paper, RGPPM is complements with a monocular vision system to generate autonomy in the planning of the paths with geometric resistive networks.

articleTitle: Solution-processed manganese phthalocyanine thin-film transistors on plastic substrates
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this work, manganese phthalocyanine (MnPc) films obtained by spin-coating at 80 °C and used as active layer in thin-film transistors (TFTs) are presented. The TFTs used the inverted coplanar structure and were fabricated on plastic substrates. Polyethylene terephthalate was used as substrate. Spin-on glass was used as gate dielectric. The MnPc thin films were characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy and current-voltage measurements. The results agree with those reported in the literature for MnPc films. The MnPc TFTs exhibit a clear modulation of the drain current Ids with the gate voltage Vgs applied.

articleTitle: Study of Flexible Organic Photodiodes for Red Ligth Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper we present relevant work on red-applied organic photodiodes fabricated on flexible substrates. Also the selection of the correct substrate helps in the application and the improvement of the device over devices with rigid substrates. We mention the most used and favorable substrates for the application of organic photodiodes in the red direction of the electromagnetic spectrum and, finally, simulations of the external quantum efficiency and spectral response are shown.

articleTitle: Fractal and Grapical Approach in Arrhytmia Pre-Diagnosis ECG Based
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)

authors.preferredName: Alvaro Gabriel Vega de la Garza

abstract: In this paper, an ECG analysis applied to a database ECG signals is done by R/S fractal algorithm transformation, and its graphical approach applied to arrhythmias pre-diagnosis is settled based in confidence-intervals statistical parameters. The results confirm the fractal graphical approach as a confident preliminary stage of prediagnosis with several and critical applications in public hearth health.

articleTitle: Generation of Microwave Signals by Optical Heterodyning Technique Using a Multimode Laser Diode and a Tunable DFB Laser
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper reports an alternative to generating microwave signals by using the optical heterodyne technique. The novelty of this work resides in the fact of using a Multimode Laser Diode (MLD) and a tunable Distributed Feedback laser (DFB) instead of a couple of two DFBs. This proposal is demonstrated at the simulation level by using the VPIphotonic software in the frequency range of 0–13 GHz. A Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) is used as the device that allows the selection of a single optical signal of the MLD. Afterward, this optical signal is beat with the optical signal issued of a tunable DBF allowing in this way the generation of the microwave signals. Even more, the tunability of the microwave signals is controlled by the tunable DBF. Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) parameter is used to evaluate the quality of these microwave signals exhibiting on average a value of 26 dB.

articleTitle: Red Eléctrica De Alta Tensión MFA-TDS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Electricity is the most important energy for man today, from home to industry and indeed all human activities, including communication.At this time, it is produced from the generation centers and travels long distances until it is used by the end user. The electrical energy is conducted in high voltage or voltage and less current so that there are less losses in the cable, since the resistance varies with respect to the length and diameter, and as these lines are losses of electricity due to heating.With the evolution of energies, both in their use and in their transformation, some small variables apply, since, although the energy is produced in different places depending on the nature of the resource to be transformed, it can be in the same consumption center or even further than traditional systems.Therefore, there is a need to evaluate what conditions intervene, hence the need to study load flows, since as it is known, loss abatement must be a permanent objective in the operation of current power electrical systems.

articleTitle: FPGA Board Implementation of Two Hamiltonian Conservative Chaotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work presents, for the first time in the literature, the implementation of two Hamiltonian conservative chaotic systems on an FPGA board, using two different numerical methods to solve the difference equations: the improved Euler and the fourth order Runge-Kutta. The chaotic oscillators that are implemented are two cases of four-dimensional Hamiltonian conservative chaotic systems, which are simulated by MATLAB software obtaining their four different time series. Subsequently, the two cases are digitally implemented on an FPGA board using the MATLAB/Simulink tool in conjunction with the Vivado software for the digital design of the modules in VHDL code. Finally, both the Matlab simulation and the digital emulation are compared, and the FPGA board logical resources used are presented. The original contribution of this work is the design of a digital platform capable of displaying the digital emulation of two cases of Hamiltonian conservative chaotic systems in an analog way, with the flexibility to change their initial conditions and parameters using software.

articleTitle: Determination of optimum tilt angle of photovoltaic panels with monthly variations for Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The tilt angle is one of the most important parameters for solar radiation collection in a photovoltaic panel, its optimization helps to increase the total solar radiation received. Numerous methods have been used to calculate the tilt angle around the world; unfortunately, many of these models are for fixed angles, which fail to adapt to the position of the sun throughout the year, resulting in the loss of significant amounts of irradiation that could be exploited. In this work we propose a series of optimal monthly tilt angles for the city of Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz, obtained by means of a neural network that considers day of the year, declination, and the clearness index as input variables. Its values range from 39.10° in January, in June it has its lowest value with −4.88 and ends with values of 41.18 in December. Theoretical calculations of incident irradiation on a tilted plane are also made, using the isotropic Liu-Jordan model and the anisotropic Klucher model, to make comparisons of energy reception between a surface with a fixed tilt angle equal to the latitude (18.1378°) and the proposed angles. The results show that using an isotropic method the irradiation obtained by panels with monthly angles increases 4.11% more and under the anisotropic method it increases 5.06% more. Thus, it is corroborated that it is possible to use neural networks to predict monthly tilt angles.

articleTitle: Design of a prototype for automatic lighting control in classrooms at Faculty of Accounting and Administration Xalapa based on the IoT paradigm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This research is developed within the framework of the benefit granted by Intel through the National Association of Universities and Institutions of Higher Education, which provided the Universidad Veracruzana with “Galileo” smart cards for the realization of projects under the IoT paradigm oriented to the development of intelligent campus. In this sense, and with the purpose of helping the Faculty of Accounting and Administration to advance towards automation, promoting the development of IoT projects and reaching a minimum of 90% sustainability; a prototype is proposed for the automatic control of lighting by implementing the use of the computer on a single board “Intel Galileo” along with the Devkit with WiSOL Sigfox module with operation under the IoT paradigm, which is able to automate the lighting of the classroom, and thus reduce energy consumption, administrative costs and environmental impact.

articleTitle: Development of a web-based and gender-based Participatory GIS for Perceived Public Insecurity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The perception of public insecurity as a subjective part of human safety is currently a central indicator of governments to diagnose the quality of life for people, as perceiving an unsafe place produces a behavioral adjustment that has concrete spatial expressions with consequences at the macro-social, community, and individual levels for different identities that are not sufficiently reflected as security measures at the location level. Participatory GIS (PGIS), together with gender indicators allow the co-production of knowledge from a different perspective than that coming from a hierarchical structure that reinforces binary genders and considers a single generic citizen. The present work introduces an approach to adopt web-based participatory GIS techniques along with gender perspective, and the development of an online platform to collect perceptions of insecurity and gender violence towards women applied in the Historic Center of the City of Puebla, Mexico.

articleTitle: Intervention project of the Dual Training Model at the Universidad Veracruzana
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently, there is the problem of reducing the gap between the relevance of educational programs of higher education institutions and companies, it is required, that the incorporation to the productive sector by graduates is carried out easily, reducing induction times and costs, allowing have human resources with the necessary skills to occupy strategic positions in organizations. The objective of this research is to present the proposed intervention of the Dual Training Model at the Universidad Veracruzana, a higher-level educational institution in Mexico, which was implemented in the second semester of 2020 with the incorporation of last semester students to previously said model. A non-experimental, exploratory and descriptive research was carried out under a conceptual and theoretical methodology that allowed to carry out the conceptualization obtaining the results and then, formalize the model, considering the national and international initiatives that have been successfully adapting them to the socio-economic characteristics of the institution and its surroundings. As a result of the research, it can be affirmed that currently, the Universidad Veracruzana has a Dual Training Model, a situation that will allow an assessment of the relevance of educational programs, this being an alternative to reduce the aforementioned gap.

articleTitle: Use of weighted graphs in simulation to administrate waste collection system
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work addresses the problem of the administration of wastes within the Facultad de Negocios y Tecnologías, located in the city of Ixtaczoquitlan, Veracruz. In this work, the simulations of garbage generation and collection have been done, this in order to increase the efficiency in the collection as well as the administration of resources, in this case, the time needed to collect the garbage. This work, after waste generation simulation, applies intelligent path planning algorithms as the main component to solve the problem, uses topological maps as input, with this, the algorithm is capable of generating the optimal collection route in a matter of shorter path. As a result of the use of these algorithms, it can be verified that the prioritized routes done after apply the algorithm can be shorter than the current route, which is to do the whole route.

articleTitle: FPGA Realization of Image Encryption System with Chaotic Attractors: Two-Wings and Jerk
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article carries out the FPGA implementation of an information encryption system using chaos. First, the discrete numerical methods of Improved Euler and Runge-Kutta of the fourth order are used to solve the differential equations that describe two chaotic oscillator models: Two-Wings and Jerk. Subsequently, the performance and use of logical resources are compared in order to find the numerical method that is most efficient due to the limited amount of resources that an FPGA has. The contributions of this work are a simulator and a modular image encryption system with encrypted-decrypted correlation coefficients of less than 1 and a low consumption of logical resources.

articleTitle: An analytical method to model the IDS of the MOSFET transistor using a graphene channel
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: One of the biggest problems in the scale of the MOSFET, has been the short channel effect. A viable alternative that has become very relevant nowadays, is the graphene used as a channel, due to its electrical properties, decreases the negative effects that limit the performance of the devices when exchanging the existing silice technology, to scale to other technologies, with the opportunity to develop devices with thinner channels that allow us the MOSFETs to reach shorter lengths of channel with higher speeds. This material opened a new path in the study of transmission and transport properties in two-dimensional systems, which makes it relevant to work in modeling based on these properties. In this work, a review of the MOSFETs with graphene channel made in recent years, and modeling of the drain source current, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf>, with a single-layer graphene channel through a methodological analysis of the engineering of current behavior are presented.

articleTitle: Project PE-A-06 CEMIE Redes : Part 1: Characterization and Estimation of Technical Power Losses in Low-Voltage Electric Networks of Mexico Using Analysis and Measurement Tools
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the advances and results of a research project conducted by the Mexican Centre of Innovation in Intelligent Electrical Networks and Micro-networks (CEMIE-Redes) funded by the 2138 Sectorial Fund CONACYT-SENER-Sustainable Energy. The main objective is to know the technical power losses associated with the different areas, which integrate low voltage electric networks in Mexico. Since there are about 1.5 million low-voltage networks in Mexico, a census is not feasible, therefore a sampling approach is followed. The statistical algorithms for the selection of a sample were developed and implemented in a computer system. Measurement equipment will be installed in the sampled networks for collecting data, which will be used to estimate nationwide the total technical loss and, via mathematical models, to calculate the technical losses in each low voltage network of the national energy distribution system.
